<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:emoreward" data-paper-title="EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-emoreward-0937a172" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ff355c3308b0e3ed">If a facial provider correlated strongly with the proxy outcome in the previous run, should it still get reward weight for a video with no usable face?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aemoreward">EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-07 · The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The historical multiplier changes relative weights among usable providers. The current gate controls availability. A zero gate gives zero effective weight regardless of the multiplier.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: A facial channel with base weight 0.4 and historical multiplier 2 still has zero effective weight when its gate is 0. A neutral default is not an observation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06518">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.06518-emoreward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ff355c3308b0e3ed">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:emoreward" data-paper-title="EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8b1fee98de66e2f2">Why does RewardMemory correlate raw scores with outcomes, then subtract the provider mean and clip?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aemoreward">EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-07 · The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Using raw scores rather than gated contributions avoids mistaking the previous gating policy for provider reliability. Centering expresses relative reliability, and clipping bounds log multipliers. A constant provider has zero correlation, not necessarily a penalty. With a positive cap, its unnormalized multiplier is below 1 only when the mean correlation is positive.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: Correlations of 0.8 and 0 average to 0.4. At temperature 0.5 and cap 1, their unnormalized multipliers are exp(0.8) and exp(-0.8).</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06518">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.06518-emoreward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8b1fee98de66e2f2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:emoreward" data-paper-title="EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e0032c24f08544d9">EmoReward and TVRL both support video reinforcement learning. Do they change the same training quantity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aemoreward">EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-07 · The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. EmoReward changes how emotion scores are fused into a scalar for each video. TVRL starts from an existing group advantage and redistributes credit according to a frozen VLM&#x27;s sensitivity to generation tokens. One does not substitute for the other.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: EmoReward can ignore a missing face score, while TVRL can allocate more of an existing advantage to influential tokens in the same trajectory. These changes operate along different axes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 诊断与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06518">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.06518-emoreward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e0032c24f08544d9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:emoreward" data-paper-title="EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3b23dc7568601157">Why does Eq. (8) apply the active threshold before normalization? May the current outcome update the table at runtime?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aemoreward">EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-07 · The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The threshold applies to the product w⁰gm, not its normalized version, and equality is excluded. Normalize only over the selected providers. The current outcome cannot refit the frozen table; the next run reads a table constructed after a separate reference run has finished.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: Effective weights (0.25, 1, 0) and a threshold of 0.25 keep only the second provider. If every gate is zero, the emotion term is zero, but the general video reward can still contribute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06518">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.06518-emoreward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3b23dc7568601157">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dars-density" data-paper-title="Density-Aware Reward Scaling: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Reward-Proportional Sampling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-dars-density-18c61412" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7bc30bb50cef9df3">Why does DARS correct rewards in outcome-representation space rather than merely increase action entropy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adars-density">Density-Aware Reward Scaling: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Reward-Proportional Sampling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Random actions need not cover several terminal modes. Different rewrites can produce similar images. DARS reduces the relative reward of crowded outcome regions within one prompt group, targeting terminal coverage rather than simply randomizing each action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: Ten different wordings all produce the same sunset composition. Prompt vocabulary is diverse but image modes still collapse; image-embedding density can reveal this crowding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04792">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.04792-dars/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7bc30bb50cef9df3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dars-density" data-paper-title="Density-Aware Reward Scaling: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Reward-Proportional Sampling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4ac0f25bbc00d4e8">Why must Gaussian KDE retain self terms, and what happens to duplicates at narrow bandwidth?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adars-density">Density-Aware Reward Scaling: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Reward-Proportional Sampling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The sum includes every group member, including a self contribution of one, so density is at least one. Narrow bandwidth suppresses contributions between distinct points, not coincident points. Duplicates retain their multiplicity; removing self or setting every density to one changes rewards.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: Outcomes (0,0,100) at h=.001 have densities (2,2,1). Unit rewards become (.5,.5,1). Narrow bandwidth does not make the two coincident points invisible to one another.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 检查与负控. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04792">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.04792-dars/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4ac0f25bbc00d4e8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dars-density" data-paper-title="Density-Aware Reward Scaling: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Reward-Proportional Sampling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-82b02e5f4fdd79fe">When does wide bandwidth reduce to GRPO, and why still declare the standard-deviation convention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adars-density">Density-Aware Reward Scaling: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Reward-Proportional Sampling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>When all densities approach the same G, their common reward scale cancels under the same standard-deviation convention, recovering ordinary group normalization. Population versus sample deviation changes advantage scale. The paper leaves this unspecified, so the local choice must be explicit rather than presented as an algorithmic gain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: For G=3, sample deviation is sqrt(3/2) times population deviation, scaling advantages by sqrt(2/3). This is a convention difference, not less mode collapse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 检查与负控. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04792">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.04792-dars/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-82b02e5f4fdd79fe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dars-density" data-paper-title="Density-Aware Reward Scaling: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Reward-Proportional Sampling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d7e97293505334a0">Why not mix densities across prompts, and why stop gradients through outcomes and rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adars-density">Density-Aware Reward Scaling: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Reward-Proportional Sampling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>DARS measures crowding within one conditioning input&#x27;s rollout group. Mixing prompts penalizes outcomes under unrelated conditions. The component processes policy-gradient rewards, not gradients through frozen image encoders or rewards. Zero-variance groups explicitly return zero advantages or raise instead of hiding the issue with epsilon.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: A cat prompt and a car prompt can yield similar backgrounds without needing to suppress each other&#x27;s rewards. A frozen feature passed with requires_grad=True must still receive no gradient from advantage processing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 实现与运行, 检查与负控. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04792">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.04792-dars/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d7e97293505334a0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mart-grpo" data-paper-title="When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-mart-grpo-1903b786" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d10e4667ff1e98b4">Why mask late feedback on MART-GRPO failures?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amart-grpo">When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal failure doesn&#x27;t mean every later action caused it. Find the last unrecovered error and mask subsequent negative credit while retaining relevant earlier signal; execution itself is not stopped early.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A failed regrasp after a drop needn&#x27;t be punished equally solely because the episode failed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32431v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.32431-mart-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d10e4667ff1e98b4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mart-grpo" data-paper-title="When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e7694d8cca75156c">Why keep original advantages and denominator after masking penalties beyond the last unrecovered error?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amart-grpo">When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Masking isolates where failure credit applies. Changing group rewards/advantages or denominator adds other effects. Execute whole rollout before VLM hindsight; that does not guarantee stopping-time theory applies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mask idle behavior after a mishap without amplifying punishment for the remaining actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32431v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.32431-mart-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e7694d8cca75156c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mart-grpo" data-paper-title="When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8ac75269276a736b">Why isn&#x27;t a retrospective VLM boundary automatically a theoretical stopping time?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amart-grpo">When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The VLM sees future trajectory, unlike a decision based only on the past. Arbitrary masks don&#x27;t inherit unbiasedness or variance reduction guarantees.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choosing an important step after seeing the outcome differs from deciding as it happens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32431v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.32431-mart-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8ac75269276a736b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mart-grpo" data-paper-title="When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9bd0021c9f561f87">May MART recompute advantages or renormalize by unmasked tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amart-grpo">When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Keep original group advantages and valid-action denominator; apply the mask only to feedback. Valid interval includes its upper endpoint. Invalid format/identity/bounds are errors, not semantic-uncertainty fallback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Shrinking the denominator after masking amplifies retained gradients and changes the method.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32431v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.32431-mart-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9bd0021c9f561f87">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mge-po" data-paper-title="MGE-PO: Entropy-Aware Credit Assignment for Mathematical Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-mge-po-5743f3b7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-53cb1c4c12782d8b">Are MGE-PO success/failure and high/low entropy the same label?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amge-po">MGE-PO: Entropy-Aware Credit Assignment for Mathematical Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构（不据邮箱域名推断）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Verified outcome and policy uncertainty are distinct axes; all four combinations occur. Entropy alone is not correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A model can confidently be wrong or hesitate and get it right.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23245v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.23245-mge-po/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-53cb1c4c12782d8b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mge-po" data-paper-title="MGE-PO: Entropy-Aware Credit Assignment for Mathematical Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bdfc8a5d4d1b5197">Why use generation-time cached entropy rather than recalculate after an update?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amge-po">MGE-PO: Entropy-Aware Credit Assignment for Mathematical Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构（不据邮箱域名推断）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Credit describes uncertainty at sampling. New policy entropy would mix policy changes into old trajectory judgment. Combine outcome and entropy quadrants with separate curriculum/KL; truncated replies can still shift through recentering.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A reply becoming more certain after training was not necessarily sampled confidently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23245v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.23245-mge-po/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bdfc8a5d4d1b5197">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mge-po" data-paper-title="MGE-PO: Entropy-Aware Credit Assignment for Mathematical Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-63a80fb16094e7b5">How do MGE-PO quadrants differ from rewarding low entropy alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amge-po">MGE-PO: Entropy-Aware Credit Assignment for Mathematical Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构（不据邮箱域名推断）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Combine outcome with entropy; confidence is not inherently good. Low-entropy reward alone can reinforce confident errors. Verifiable correctness is needed without leaking evaluation gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Low-entropy correct and low-entropy wrong replies need different credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23245v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.23245-mge-po/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-63a80fb16094e7b5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mge-po" data-paper-title="MGE-PO: Entropy-Aware Credit Assignment for Mathematical Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-65e6ce7ff69955ff">Why can a truncated response have nonzero final advantage after zero direct correction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amge-po">MGE-PO: Entropy-Aware Credit Assignment for Mathematical Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构（不据邮箱域名推断）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Zero direct increment doesn&#x27;t prevent batch recentering from moving all advantages. Use lagged problem EMA for curriculum and cached sampling-policy entropy, not future generations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Positive corrections on peers shift the mean and move an uncorrected reply relatively.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23245v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.23245-mge-po/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-65e6ce7ff69955ff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tag-reward-gating" data-paper-title="Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-tag-reward-gating-d0312c36" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7568ec547fc88e46">Why choose a reliable anchor before TAG multi-reward training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atag-reward-gating">Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of British Columbia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Auxiliary objectives can be gamed while harming the main goal. Enable auxiliary credit only when the anchor is met; this differs from shrinking its coefficient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A short incorrect answer shouldn&#x27;t get positive brevity credit on its own.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21404v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21404-tag-reward-gating/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7568ec547fc88e46">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tag-reward-gating" data-paper-title="Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a30ff0ff404f806">Why discard anchor probes and restart, and when do auxiliary rewards apply?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atag-reward-gating">Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of British Columbia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate probes measure reward-induced drift, not supply final weights. Restart from the common baseline to isolate selection. Anchor failure blocks auxiliary credit. Sample under each probe to preserve KL direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Brevity can&#x27;t raise credit on an incorrect answer if correctness is the anchor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21404v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21404-tag-reward-gating/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a30ff0ff404f806">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tag-reward-gating" data-paper-title="Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f580247c5dd0e8fc">How does TAG&#x27;s low-drift probe selection differ from manually selecting correctness?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atag-reward-gating">Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of British Columbia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Probe each reward from the same baseline, choose via probe-to-baseline reverse KL, discard probes and retrain. A manually chosen anchor skips that process.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fast reward growth can cause large drift, not make it the chosen anchor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21404v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21404-tag-reward-gating/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f580247c5dd0e8fc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tag-reward-gating" data-paper-title="Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-97ee3549d16b5442">Why estimate TAG drift on each probe&#x27;s own trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atag-reward-gating">Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of British Columbia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reverse-KL expectation is under the probe. Baseline sampling changes direction. Pool all generated tokens, not per-response means. A finite-sample estimate may be negative; do not clamp.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Long and short responses contribute their tokens jointly rather than equal response weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21404v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21404-tag-reward-gating/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-97ee3549d16b5442">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sif" data-paper-title="Learning to Reason with Selective Internal Feedback" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-sif-620fc6b5" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f888a406df8ca361">Why not treat mean self-certainty as a correct label in SIF?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asif">Learning to Reason with Selective Internal Feedback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Confidence may grow for wrong answers. Compare ranked certainty windows across same-prompt replies, then use two-level voting for relative reward. This is not independent truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A confident error does not become right due to a high mean.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21392v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21392-sif/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f888a406df8ca361">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sif" data-paper-title="Learning to Reason with Selective Internal Feedback" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-560ca2565f6d2582">Why compare sorted certainty windows instead of using entropy or high-probability tokens as labels?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asif">Learning to Reason with Selective Internal Feedback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mean confidence can amplify errors. Build a profile using uniform-to-policy KL, then compare eligible same-prompt replies at window and peer levels. This is not entropy or sampled probability; filter ineligible/equal-reward groups and share policy/KL masks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Multiple windows distinguish a few extreme positions from broadly uniform certainty.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21392v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21392-sif/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-560ca2565f6d2582">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sif" data-paper-title="Learning to Reason with Selective Internal Feedback" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7db75046cdac1089">Why isn&#x27;t SIF&#x27;s KL(U||π) negative entropy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asif">Learning to Reason with Selective Internal Feedback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It averages log probabilities uniformly; negative entropy weights by policy probabilities. Direction and low-probability sensitivity differ, as does using only sampled tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A rare token approaching zero affects uniform-to-policy KL differently from policy-weighted entropy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21392v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21392-sif/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7db75046cdac1089">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sif" data-paper-title="Learning to Reason with Selective Internal Feedback" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-743b1654ab9a1908">Should ineligible SIF replies disable KL as well?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asif">Learning to Reason with Selective Internal Feedback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Yes. Policy and KL use the same selection mask. Keep original response normalization, eligibility, strict comparisons and sample SD. A tie isn&#x27;t a win.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Turning off policy loss but retaining KL would still update a filtered response.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21392v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21392-sif/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-743b1654ab9a1908">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:progress-reward" data-paper-title="Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-progress-reward-e17dc6a6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-43d964b36c94f1d8">Why does PRM4RL provide subtask semantics and a progress potential?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprogress-reward">Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Subtask meaning enriches state with current phase; potential differences supply dense progress despite sparse terminal success. One changes inputs, the other rewards, and planning can be offline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A robot knows it is grasping and receives progress for moving closer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22056v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.22056-progress-reward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-43d964b36c94f1d8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:progress-reward" data-paper-title="Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d43537bb6eddd8b">Why use discounted potential differences and not treat timeout as termination?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprogress-reward">Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Neighbor terms telescope to endpoints. Correct absorbing boundary prevents terminal potential changing the objective. A timeout may leave future progress possible, so don&#x27;t zero it automatically. Subtask encoding and shaping remain independent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Zeroing potential when time expires near a goal can fabricate a progress penalty.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22056v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.22056-progress-reward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d43537bb6eddd8b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:progress-reward" data-paper-title="Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4057a09262779abf">How does potential shaping differ from rewarding raw progress at each step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprogress-reward">Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Discounted differences compare transitions and telescope, while repeated high potential can reward idling. Terminal conditions matter; differencing alone does not guarantee policy invariance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Staying at a high-progress state without finishing can accrue reward under raw per-step scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22056v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.22056-progress-reward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4057a09262779abf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:progress-reward" data-paper-title="Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-94810a2cf81ad696">Why distinguish true termination from time truncation in PRM4RL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprogress-reward">Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An absorbing terminal can have zero potential; time-limited states can retain successor value. Use the formula absent explicit termination and review generated functions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Timeout with a resumable task differs from actual success or failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opcredit" data-paper-title="OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-opcredit-fae57ef0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-467f3a76765e0009">Why assign OpCredit search credit to individual operations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopcredit">OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Successful trajectories can detour and failed ones can explore usefully. Branch outcomes and frontier changes score local operations, then align generated reasoning/action tokens, not environment observations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Finding a key entity can be useful even if the final answer fails.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21345v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21345-opcredit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-467f3a76765e0009">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opcredit" data-paper-title="OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b7d3d7888c5e21b5">Why match visited set, remaining budget and phase when comparing operations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopcredit">OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The same entity can have different future opportunities. BOC matches context and deduplicates by trajectory; FTC uses training answer neighborhoods for local improvement. Keep answers out of actor input and observations out of policy loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two visits to one node differ if only one has explored its neighbors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21345v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21345-opcredit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b7d3d7888c5e21b5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opcredit" data-paper-title="OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9c6efe2251e4b589">What does BOC branch comparison use versus FTC frontier progress?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopcredit">OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>BOC reuses outcomes from matched states; FTC assesses local frontier against a training-only answer neighborhood. Training labels can score credit afterward but remain hidden during sampling. They are distinct signals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Closeness to the training answer may score a neighbor after rollout, never enter the search request.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21345v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21345-opcredit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9c6efe2251e4b589">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opcredit" data-paper-title="OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ddad88751e9efaa5">Why not match OpCredit branches by active entity alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopcredit">OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Match problem, visited set, budget and phase to compare similar opportunities. Count each trajectory once. FTC uses the frontier&#x27;s best chance, not graph-wide mean distance. Detach credit and reference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Arriving with no budget differs from arriving with resources to search.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21345v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21345-opcredit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ddad88751e9efaa5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mrtpo" data-paper-title="Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-mrtpo-6e178dc9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-82c09b1f0f2ccc05">Why not broadcast every MRTPO reward equally over a response?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amrtpo">Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Minnesota</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Format, executability and correctness can depend on different tokens. Removing one information block and measuring distribution shift identifies likely relevant positions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>SQL grammar and numerical correctness may point to different tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21439v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21439-mrtpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-82c09b1f0f2ccc05">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mrtpo" data-paper-title="Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ff72edc10ba95a02">Why compare vocabulary-wide JS after removing each reward block?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amrtpo">Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Minnesota</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A sampled token may miss movement among other candidates. Full-distribution changes associate reward information with positions. Mean-preserving weights apply to both signs with bounded magnitude. Verifier context belongs only in training replay.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing SQL-format feedback may shift mass between comma and parenthesis while the sampled token is unchanged.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21439v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21439-mrtpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ff72edc10ba95a02">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mrtpo" data-paper-title="Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4141e1fd3e3b3403">How does information ablation differ from sampled-token probability changes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amrtpo">Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Minnesota</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use full-vocabulary JS under the same frozen policy. A single token can miss mass redistribution. Association is not causal correctness, and reward info cannot enter original student sampling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The sampled token may stay constant while alternative probabilities move.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21439v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21439-mrtpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4141e1fd3e3b3403">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mrtpo" data-paper-title="Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7288bd2955058951">Why use uniform ones when all MRTPO relevance is zero?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amrtpo">Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Minnesota</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If localization is unavailable, uniform weights retain total credit. Keep response mean one before second-moment limits and batch normalization. Zeros delete the objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An empty format block should not erase the format advantage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21439v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21439-mrtpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7288bd2955058951">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:knowgpo" data-paper-title="KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-knowgpo-346974ee" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-791c6625a80c5167">Why group KnowGPO steps by known fact sets?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aknowgpo">KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different queries/pages can yield the same knowledge. Verified atomic conditions build a monotone state, enabling comparisons of what actions add from a common start.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Different wording can establish the same person and year and share a pre-state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22331v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.22331-knowgpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-791c6625a80c5167">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:knowgpo" data-paper-title="KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-99b78cf2f318ca24">Why group by pre-action knowledge rather than post-action knowledge?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aknowgpo">KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use shared initial facts to compare action benefits without conditioning on gains. A training verifier monotonically accumulates facts; combine process/terminal advantages for generated tokens only, hiding checklist from the actor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Grouping a successful and unsuccessful search by resulting facts separates the two outcomes before comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22331v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.22331-knowgpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-99b78cf2f318ca24">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:knowgpo" data-paper-title="KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6a9ae4caad7bf46a">Why not group KnowGPO by state after the action?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aknowgpo">KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Credit compares actions from a common starting point. Grouping by outcome separates actions that add different facts. Follow algorithmic pre-state despite prose ambiguity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An action finding a new fact should be compared to a miss from the same known facts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22331v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.22331-knowgpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6a9ae4caad7bf46a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:knowgpo" data-paper-title="KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6360eec115845831">How handle KnowGPO answer steps and tool observations in loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aknowgpo">KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Answer steps skip process grouping but keep the terminal mixture term. Advantage covers generated reasoning/actions only. Keep verifier facts and tool observations out of actor targets. Singleton process advantage is zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Environment search results are not model-generated tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22331v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.22331-knowgpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6360eec115845831">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:diverge-ideation" data-paper-title="Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-diverge-ideation-5eb53208" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb97cf6a3bc21812">Why generate a whole idea set instead of sampling independently and deduplicating?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adiverge-ideation">Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · New York University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Later ideas see predecessors and can seek genuinely different directions. Reward combines quality and dissimilarity. Different strings do not prove scientific novelty; semantic judging matters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A second approach can cover a gap rather than paraphrase the first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22324v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.22324-diverge-ideation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb97cf6a3bc21812">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:diverge-ideation" data-paper-title="Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-06a668f3c7600605">Why preserve generated order when assigning DIVERGE diversity credit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adiverge-ideation">Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · New York University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each idea sees preceding ideas, so nearest predecessor reflects its actual choice. Reordering changes credit. Evaluation&#x27;s discounted reordered metric is separate; semantic distance and quality need independent judging.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A second paraphrase deserves lower novelty under the original order; rearranging does not rewrite its training reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
