<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:diverge-ideation" data-paper-title="Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a1be5157fe404d78">Can DIVERGE training set reward and evaluated Creative Utility be exchanged?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adiverge-ideation">Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · New York University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Training uses distance to the closest predecessor in generation order; evaluation can reorder, discount and normalize. Greedy evaluation is only a lower bound on maximum CU.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Moving the best idea first can alter evaluation but doesn&#x27;t change original training order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22324v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.22324-diverge-ideation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a1be5157fe404d78">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:diverge-ideation" data-paper-title="Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-01e29eab2dc9e08a">Which fields count toward DIVERGE length penalties?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adiverge-ideation">Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · New York University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Count tokens in problem_gap, core_claim and method, not inspiration or think, using the intended tokenizer. Schema failure gives zero without a judge call. Character count isn&#x27;t a substitute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A long inspiration citation isn&#x27;t part of the specified length term.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rap-walk" data-paper-title="When Pairwise Preferences Cycle: A Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk for Video GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-rap-walk-742b8b38" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a29913380a281c97">Why retain opponent identity and preference cycles in RAP-Walk?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arap-walk">When Pairwise Preferences Cycle: A Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk for Video GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 未确认（已读 arXiv HTML 未列机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Win rate loses who was beaten and where preferences conflict. Edge clarity and cycle reliability inform graph credit. Cycles can reflect multi-dimensional tradeoffs, not poor samples.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A can win on motion, B visuals and C adherence, forming a meaningful cycle.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20089v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.20089-rap-walk/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a29913380a281c97">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rap-walk" data-paper-title="When Pairwise Preferences Cycle: A Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk for Video GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6be900bea95718dd">Why keep cyclic preferences instead of removing or labeling their videos bad?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arap-walk">When Pairwise Preferences Cycle: A Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk for Video GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 未确认（已读 arXiv HTML 未列机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cycles can come from different strengths. Preserve opponent identities, edge clarity and cycle inconsistency, propagate reliably from losers to winners and adjust win-rate credit. Keep direction, convergence and entropy protocol; ordinary PageRank differs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A beats B, B beats C and C beats A across visual quality, motion and adherence; deleting all loses comparisons.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20089v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.20089-rap-walk/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6be900bea95718dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rap-walk" data-paper-title="When Pairwise Preferences Cycle: A Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk for Video GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b676c0beb2f42f73">How does reliable random walk differ from averaging wins?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arap-walk">When Pairwise Preferences Cycle: A Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk for Video GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 未确认（已读 arXiv HTML 未列机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Propagate from losers to winners with reliability, obtain stationary credit and mix with a win-rate anchor. Minimum entropy prevents excessive concentration. Average wins lack that propagation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Beating opponents of different reliability does not yield identical propagated credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20089v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.20089-rap-walk/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b676c0beb2f42f73">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rap-walk" data-paper-title="When Pairwise Preferences Cycle: A Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk for Video GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-99e71ff2f73a8479">May nonconvergent RAP-Walk automatically add PageRank teleportation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arap-walk">When Pairwise Preferences Cycle: A Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk for Video GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 未确认（已读 arXiv HTML 未列机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Report failure per protocol. Use W_ji orientation, restandardize after mixing and detach preference graph/advantages. Teleportation changes stationary credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reversing loser-to-winner edges can reward opposite nodes even with a normalized matrix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20089v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.20089-rap-walk/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-99e71ff2f73a8479">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:upturn" data-paper-title="Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-upturn-1713cc09" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d3ef4642ef0f2fa1">Does UpTurn learn token edits or where to restart correction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aupturn">Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It learns paragraph cut and repair gate with frozen reasoner/encoder. Keep the prefix, insert a fixed new user turn and continue with the reasoner.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Restart after a bad derivation section instead of changing old token probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13672">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13672-upturn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d3ef4642ef0f2fa1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:upturn" data-paper-title="Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-725c5fb5bbb1c264">Why learn paragraph cuts rather than fine-tune UpTurn&#x27;s whole reasoner?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aupturn">Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freezing isolates when to insert a correction; rewards come from actual regenerated suffixes at different cuts. Keep prefix, close turn, insert fixed user turn, and obey leftover budget. It isn&#x27;t whole rewrite or model training. Gate cannot use gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retry from a paragraph boundary with less remaining budget, not unlimited free retries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13672">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13672-upturn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-725c5fb5bbb1c264">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:upturn" data-paper-title="Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-75e2b20d8166f842">How does a new dialogue turn differ from appending reflection to the assistant message?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aupturn">Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Role and conditioning boundaries change. End the assistant turn, add a new user instruction and continue within remaining budget. String append doesn&#x27;t imply equivalent chat semantics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A user&#x27;s request to recheck differs from the assistant continuing to reflect.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13672">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13672-upturn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-75e2b20d8166f842">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:upturn" data-paper-title="Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-335c54c30d946d1b">Why not give UpTurn the full L_max again after cutting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aupturn">Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prefix already consumes budget; suffix gets L_max minus cut position. No parseable answer means gate zero, threshold fixed. Some mechanism seeds still fail; execution is not stable success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Full budget after a late cut gives treatment extra generation cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13672">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13672-upturn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-335c54c30d946d1b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:soar" data-paper-title="SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-soar-c6475aad" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a387e5ecd2d98831">Why require explicit source claims in SOAR answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asoar">SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University / Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Correctness alone doesn&#x27;t verify evidential dependence. Record internal recall and external retrieval separately, then test whether the claimed stream supports the answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A retrieval claim must be supported by retrieval records, not by a lucky memory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13157">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13157-soar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a387e5ecd2d98831">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:soar" data-paper-title="SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-12ee59ebf4740899">Why ignore an answer found in the nondeclared evidence stream?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asoar">SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University / Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A declared source should actually support the answer; cross-stream rescue would reward invented dependency. Separate recall/retrieval, keep old reasoning and external evidence out of recall, and exclude observations from actor actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a reply cites retrieval but only recall contains the fact, provenance is inconsistent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13157">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13157-soar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-12ee59ebf4740899">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:soar" data-paper-title="SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-96979c3c6b6830da">Why can&#x27;t SOAR internal recall see prior reasoning or retrieval?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asoar">SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University / Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The audit distinguishes existing knowledge from external findings. Isolate recall before external evidence; contamination invalidates source matching.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Recalling a fact after reading a webpage isn&#x27;t independent memory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13157">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13157-soar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-96979c3c6b6830da">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:soar" data-paper-title="SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b7b5b84db8f01af1">Can SOAR award matching credit from the other evidence stream?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asoar">SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University / Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Check only the declared stream. Tool observations and recall text aren&#x27;t actor-loss actions. Explicitly normalize reward before group advantage; mechanism execution isn&#x27;t external capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If an answer claims recall but only a webpage supports it, correctness doesn&#x27;t earn source credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13157">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13157-soar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b7b5b84db8f01af1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:residual-advantage" data-paper-title="Residual Advantage: Student-Relative Teacher Guidance for RL with Verifiable Rewards" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-residual-advantage-393aad16" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-95133b8bdb919c25">Why turn teacher–student probability residuals into local advantages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aresidual-advantage">Residual Advantage: Student-Relative Teacher Guidance for RL with Verifiable Rewards</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Engineering University / Tencent / Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher differences supply dense guidance. Subtract the student-distribution expectation to get relative local credit, then combine with verifier advantages rather than only terminal teacher scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher preferring another word at the same prefix suggests a local update.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11519">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11519-residual-advantage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-95133b8bdb919c25">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:residual-advantage" data-paper-title="Residual Advantage: Student-Relative Teacher Guidance for RL with Verifiable Rewards" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1982982d6084b49f">Why subtract expected residual under the student and then center per response?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aresidual-advantage">Residual Advantage: Student-Relative Teacher Guidance for RL with Verifiable Rewards</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Engineering University / Tencent / Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Raw differences depend on student coverage. Student expectation yields relative local credit; response centering separates positional effects. Add to verifier advantage, not replace it. Fix scoring across the batch and refresh teacher only next round.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One word&#x27;s positive residual isn&#x27;t sufficient if alternatives have similarly positive residuals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11519">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11519-residual-advantage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1982982d6084b49f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:residual-advantage" data-paper-title="Residual Advantage: Student-Relative Teacher Guidance for RL with Verifiable Rewards" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-784c243a2fc82976">How do residual advantages differ from full-distribution KL distillation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aresidual-advantage">Residual Advantage: Student-Relative Teacher Guidance for RL with Verifiable Rewards</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Engineering University / Tencent / Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Bound and center local advantages to feed policy updates, while KL directly constrains distribution differences. Gradients and reward combination differ despite using teacher probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Subtract student expectation and response mean rather than copying logits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11519">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11519-residual-advantage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-784c243a2fc82976">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:residual-advantage" data-paper-title="Residual Advantage: Student-Relative Teacher Guidance for RL with Verifiable Rewards" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2fa1b9bb8cbdadff">Why can&#x27;t Co-RA change teachers midway through a scored batch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aresidual-advantage">Residual Advantage: Student-Relative Teacher Guidance for RL with Verifiable Rewards</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Engineering University / Tencent / Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Student/teacher consume the same scored batch. Teacher LoRA uses fixed verifier advantages, and the new teacher is used next round. Relabeling midway changes targets and provenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Old teacher on the first half and updated teacher on the second is not fixed supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11519">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11519-residual-advantage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2fa1b9bb8cbdadff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tvrl" data-paper-title="Token-Level Video Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-tvrl-0c541634" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-017b1a45c76fbcfd">Why use gradient sensitivity for video-token credit in TVRL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atvrl">Token-Level Video Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal video reward is coarse. Sensitivity through a frozen evaluator localizes group advantage. Sensitivity means response to perturbations, not verified correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Action terms may affect video reward more than connective words.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01973">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.01973-tvrl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-017b1a45c76fbcfd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tvrl" data-paper-title="Token-Level Video Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-52574986269291c8">Why interpret high VLM-reward gradient as sensitivity rather than correct credit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atvrl">Token-Level Video Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It measures local response of the current reward function. Mean-normalized token reweighting controls scale, but shortcut-driven sensitivities need not be causal. Local checks neither train videos nor prove perception gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A corner watermark can receive a large gradient without being a route to better video quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01973">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.01973-tvrl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-52574986269291c8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tvrl" data-paper-title="Token-Level Video Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-344d709eb000f913">How does TVRL sensitivity differ from uniformly broadcasting advantage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atvrl">Token-Level Video Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalized gradient norms emphasize sensitive positions while uniform credits ignore them. Quality depends on the frozen VLM; gradients alone are not causal evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Evaluator sensitivity to a word can be a shortcut.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01973">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.01973-tvrl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-344d709eb000f913">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tvrl" data-paper-title="Token-Level Video Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7e0532299250133a">Does local TVRL train a video diffusion model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atvrl">Token-Level Video Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It computes gradient-based credits and mean normalization. Real video, frozen VLM gradients and policy training remain; handle all-zero norms explicitly. Random inputs are not video capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Hand-supplied gradient sizes validate weighting without generating videos.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01973">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.01973-tvrl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7e0532299250133a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:my-fault" data-paper-title="My FAULT: Self-Diagnosis as Credit Assignment in Self-Evolving Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-my-fault-cefa1f11" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e739d97e21fc937">Why verify My FAULT self-diagnoses before pricing errors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amy-fault">My FAULT: Self-Diagnosis as Credit Assignment in Self-Evolving Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Self-explanations can invent causes. Only evidence-supported categories/locations enter online pricing; relative costs allocate terminal credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A claim that the tool failed needs trace evidence before penalizing tool steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01161">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.01161-my-fault/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e739d97e21fc937">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:my-fault" data-paper-title="My FAULT: Self-Diagnosis as Credit Assignment in Self-Evolving Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a0aa95a3d7af3e5">Why verify diagnostic claims before error pricing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amy-fault">My FAULT: Self-Diagnosis as Credit Assignment in Self-Evolving Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hindsight explanations can rationalize. Evidence-verified location and class drive relative online prices and conserved terminal credit redistribution. No invented success reward or jointly trained local diagnosis model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If search was correct but summary dropped a fact, don&#x27;t penalize search merely because the model blames it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01161">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.01161-my-fault/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a0aa95a3d7af3e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:my-fault" data-paper-title="My FAULT: Self-Diagnosis as Credit Assignment in Self-Evolving Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ad19140e9b0328c6">How does conserved redistribution differ from an extra error penalty?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amy-fault">My FAULT: Self-Diagnosis as Credit Assignment in Self-Evolving Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Conservation preserves total terminal return and changes only allocation. Extra penalties change the objective and incentives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Lower one step&#x27;s credit and offset elsewhere rather than deduct from the entire return twice.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01161">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.01161-my-fault/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ad19140e9b0328c6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:my-fault" data-paper-title="My FAULT: Self-Diagnosis as Credit Assignment in Self-Evolving Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-22cc52b5d633b695">What conservation invariant should My FAULT check?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amy-fault">My FAULT: Self-Diagnosis as Credit Assignment in Self-Evolving Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Valid-step credits sum to original return. Mean cost and step count use the same mask. Local screening/cost/conservation does not jointly train a policy and diagnosis model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Including padding in mean cost breaks conservation on valid steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01161">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.01161-my-fault/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-22cc52b5d633b695">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:carm" data-paper-title="CARM: Cancellation-Aware Response Masking for LLM Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-carm-c2bacd93" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d62623fa8b57200">Why take absolute token log ratios in CARM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acarm">CARM: Cancellation-Aware Response Masking for LLM Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Moore Threads AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Signed shifts can cancel across positions and conceal severe drift. Average absolute magnitude and use a response-level gate to detect cancellation risk.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sharp rise at one token and equal fall at another can average to zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02039">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.02039-carm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d62623fa8b57200">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:carm" data-paper-title="CARM: Cancellation-Aware Response Masking for LLM Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8bd0cdb80dceafcc">Why take absolute log ratios before response averaging?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acarm">CARM: Cancellation-Aware Response Masking for LLM Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Moore Threads AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Opposing probability shifts can cancel in a normal sequence mean. Absolute averaging detects magnitude and masks large mismatch. It measures policy shift, not answer quality, with a detached gate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Opposite shifts across sentence halves produce near-zero total signed drift but large mean absolute drift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02039">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.02039-carm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8bd0cdb80dceafcc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:carm" data-paper-title="CARM: Cancellation-Aware Response Masking for LLM Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c46d61ebc67a055">How does CARM differ from filtering on geometric ratio near one?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acarm">CARM: Cancellation-Aware Response Masking for LLM Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Moore Threads AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Geometric ratios allow signed cancellation; CARM measures unsigned change and can reject internally shifted responses near ratio one. This is not quality scoring.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A balanced ledger can still hide large cash movements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:carm" data-paper-title="CARM: Cancellation-Aware Response Masking for LLM Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5e16cfa5082016de">Should CARM differentiate through the response gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acarm">CARM: Cancellation-Aware Response Masking for LLM Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Moore Threads AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Freeze selection, measure valid response tokens only and apply the specified threshold. No Qwen3.5 training or measured stability improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Don&#x27;t add gradients through a threshold recomputed from updated probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02039">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.02039-carm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5e16cfa5082016de">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:t2spo" data-paper-title="T2SPO: Trajectory-to-Step Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-t2spo-3a6c006a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-140748fa5efbfd50">Why use remaining steps in successful traces as T2SPO distance?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3At2spo">T2SPO: Trajectory-to-Step Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Successful history offers state/remaining-step support examples for a frozen in-context predictor, giving denser progress than terminal success. Failure cannot be relabeled as close to success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A state three steps from completion provides a support label.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00388">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.00388-t2spo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-140748fa5efbfd50">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:t2spo" data-paper-title="T2SPO: Trajectory-to-Step Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-32febe1027d78f23">Why set successor distance to zero at success but directly zero progress at failure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3At2spo">T2SPO: Trajectory-to-Step Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Success reaches the goal; failure only stops execution, so treating it as distance zero creates false progress. Score before updating successful history to avoid leakage. Handle time truncation according to GRPO/PPO.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tool-exhaustion exit is not zero steps to success and must not reward the final failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00388">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.00388-t2spo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-32febe1027d78f23">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:t2spo" data-paper-title="T2SPO: Trajectory-to-Step Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dfa8733b74c8bb46">How does distance-improvement credit complement terminal success?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3At2spo">T2SPO: Trajectory-to-Step Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Distance differences guide intermediate steps; terminal reward still measures outcome. Mask/scale imperfect forecasts. TabPFN prediction errors don&#x27;t establish task success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An action can move toward the goal without completing it; still verify terminal result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00388">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.00388-t2spo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dfa8733b74c8bb46">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:t2spo" data-paper-title="T2SPO: Trajectory-to-Step Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1808ae2cbc70dbb5">Does T2SPO optimizer=ppo provide a full PPO trainer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3At2spo">T2SPO: Trajectory-to-Step Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It changes truncation semantics only, no critic/GAE. GRPO zeroes truncated credit; PPO uses predicted real successor. Fit standardization/SVD only on historical supports.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changing an option string does not create a value network.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00388">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.00388-t2spo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1808ae2cbc70dbb5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sharpo" data-paper-title="SHARPO: Segment-Level Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-sharpo-de267e69" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f14e021dde614f5f">Why give SHARPO a successful same-group trajectory as teacher context?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asharpo">SHARPO: Segment-Level Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Georgia Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An in-task success guides rescoring student logp within interaction segments and scales original GRPO advantage. Teacher context is training credit, not a deployment gold plan.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use a successful path to strengthen related behavior without pasting it into the inference prompt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00838">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.00838-sharpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f14e021dde614f5f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sharpo" data-paper-title="SHARPO: Segment-Level Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb132069cbbc6f92">Why use bounded scaling after rescoring segments against a successful path?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asharpo">SHARPO: Segment-Level Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Georgia Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Same-group success supplies extra context at the actual prefix. Segment logp gaps express local support. Bounded factors limit amplification and preserve original GRPO direction. Success context remains training-only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retrieval in a failed trace may resemble a successful path while synthesis diverges, so weight the two segments differently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00838">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.00838-sharpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb132069cbbc6f92">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sharpo" data-paper-title="SHARPO: Segment-Level Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a8453c1cebfd958d">How does bounded SHARPO multiplication differ from adding teacher advantage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asharpo">SHARPO: Segment-Level Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Georgia Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Twice sigmoid lies between zero and two, so scaling preserves sign and cannot turn zero nonzero. Additive terms can flip credit. The teacher modulates intensity rather than rewriting outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A failed segment can be penalized less but not rewarded merely by teacher preference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00838">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.00838-sharpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a8453c1cebfd958d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sharpo" data-paper-title="SHARPO: Segment-Level Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c8a64e5d92aa765a">What constraints apply to SHARPO segments and gold plans?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asharpo">SHARPO: Segment-Level Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Georgia Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Average teacher–student gaps within matching interaction segments and broadcast there, excluding tool observations. Local segments use no gold plan or 7B training; fixtures aren&#x27;t capability evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mixing a tool call with a different turn&#x27;s answer gives the wrong segment mean.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00838">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.00838-sharpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c8a64e5d92aa765a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pact" data-paper-title="PACT: From Credit Assignment to Critic Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-pact-439c5053" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2bcf3e2654649c91">Why tie PACT token credit to prefix value?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Apact">PACT: From Credit Assignment to Critic Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AllSpark Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One terminal reward is coarse. Prefix-conditioned expected return contextualizes it; R−V approximates advantage. Exact credit needs theoretical assumptions; a learned critic is an approximation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same failure can yield different advantages at an easy versus difficult prefix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26355">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.26355-pact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2bcf3e2654649c91">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pact" data-paper-title="PACT: From Credit Assignment to Critic Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4512977cc96eb85e">Why recompute PACT ratios after actor update, and may targets above one be clipped?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Apact">PACT: From Credit Assignment to Critic Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AllSpark Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>New/old token ratios correct old returns toward the updated actor&#x27;s critic target. The product can exceed one; clipping changes the objective. Use stable softplus and the prescribed update order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A more likely successful action after update should change critic weighting instead of fitting only old sampling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26355">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.26355-pact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4512977cc96eb85e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pact" data-paper-title="PACT: From Credit Assignment to Critic Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5734fd63ef0bee5c">Why update actor before critic in PACT instead of fitting the old policy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Apact">PACT: From Credit Assignment to Critic Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AllSpark Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The critic should follow the updated policy. Correct observed returns with a current-token new/old ratio, not an exact full-future continuation product.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Once actor actions change, replaying uncorrected old returns leaves the critic behind.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26355">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.26355-pact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5734fd63ef0bee5c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pact" data-paper-title="PACT: From Credit Assignment to Critic Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9144cf1db5f3c27f">Why not send ρR above one to ordinary probability BCE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Apact">PACT: From Credit Assignment to Critic Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AllSpark Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use the specified softplus(z)−Yz form and filter out-of-range ratios. Standard BCE may reject or alter targets outside [0,1]. Sparse nonzero local outcomes aren&#x27;t reliable gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reward one times a ratio slightly above one naturally exceeds one; do not clamp it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26355">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.26355-pact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9144cf1db5f3c27f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tiao" data-paper-title="TIAO: Token Importance-Aware Policy Optimization for Text Summarization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-tiao-f57cc707" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1daed1b1b2c11bfc">Why mask the source document in TIAO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atiao">TIAO: Token Importance-Aware Policy Optimization for Text Summarization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Defense Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Summaries should use evidence. Comparing probabilities with and without source locates evidence-sensitive tokens for trajectory/token credit. Dependence is association, not verified truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing a relevant sentence can affect a name more than a conjunction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16748">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.16748-tiao/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1daed1b1b2c11bfc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tiao" data-paper-title="TIAO: Token Importance-Aware Policy Optimization for Text Summarization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d4589e1aa50f7cf">Why use masked-source token probability changes rather than length-based credit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atiao">TIAO: Token Importance-Aware Policy Optimization for Text Summarization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Defense Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tokens vary in evidence dependence; paired scoring supplies local clues and shapes both trajectory and token credit. Length doesn&#x27;t identify provenance. Masking can itself shift distribution, so association is not factual attribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A date and a connective at similar positions need not receive the same evidence credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16748">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.16748-tiao/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d4589e1aa50f7cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tiao" data-paper-title="TIAO: Token Importance-Aware Policy Optimization for Text Summarization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc23fe1a47d3797e">How does TIAO dual-scale credit differ from one summary score?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atiao">TIAO: Token Importance-Aware Policy Optimization for Text Summarization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Defense Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Whole-summary score captures overall quality; token dependence redistributes local updates. A good aggregate doesn&#x27;t supervise every token correctly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One hallucinated date in a good summary calls for localized correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16748">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.16748-tiao/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc23fe1a47d3797e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tiao" data-paper-title="TIAO: Token Importance-Aware Policy Optimization for Text Summarization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-57c47c920b15a51d">Which response should both TIAO views score?</h2>
