<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atiao">TIAO: Token Importance-Aware Policy Optimization for Text Summarization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Defense Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use identical response and prefixes under complete/masked source. Otherwise generation changes confound the intervention. Local dependence kernel does not train the paper&#x27;s 7B model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scoring A with source and generating B without it doesn&#x27;t isolate source removal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16748">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.16748-tiao/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-57c47c920b15a51d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:spear" data-paper-title="SPEAR: Distilling Domain-Adaptive Reasoning Skeletons via Sequential Symbolic Alignment in Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-spear-64318b6a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4ce49a0d006854c3">Why convert teacher reasoning to symbolic milestones in SPEAR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspear">SPEAR: Distilling Domain-Adaptive Reasoning Skeletons via Sequential Symbolic Alignment in Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pittsburgh</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal reward is sparse and neural process judges costly. Domain milestones permit ordered alignment and dense progress, if extraction preserves important reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Match key equations rather than copying all teacher wording.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26550">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.26550-spear/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4ce49a0d006854c3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:spear" data-paper-title="SPEAR: Distilling Domain-Adaptive Reasoning Skeletons via Sequential Symbolic Alignment in Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6186a5ebb210c071">Why align milestones with LCS-F1 instead of checking the same symbols?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspear">SPEAR: Distilling Domain-Adaptive Reasoning Skeletons via Sequential Symbolic Alignment in Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pittsburgh</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Identical sets can break reasoning order. LCS preserves relative order and precision/recall detect redundancy and omissions, providing dense feedback. Extraction can err; local candidate axes are not a natural-language extractor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Substituting conditions before solving differs from writing the result then inventing conditions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26550">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.26550-spear/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6186a5ebb210c071">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:spear" data-paper-title="SPEAR: Distilling Domain-Adaptive Reasoning Skeletons via Sequential Symbolic Alignment in Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-19016356004de9ab">How does LCS-F1 differ from unordered overlap?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspear">SPEAR: Distilling Domain-Adaptive Reasoning Skeletons via Sequential Symbolic Alignment in Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pittsburgh</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>LCS respects order; F1 measures coverage and redundancy. Reordered dependencies can retain the same set yet deserve different credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Putting a conclusion before its premises can look identical to set overlap.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26550">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.26550-spear/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-19016356004de9ab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:spear" data-paper-title="SPEAR: Distilling Domain-Adaptive Reasoning Skeletons via Sequential Symbolic Alignment in Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b3521e591526d2b8">Does local SPEAR extract natural-language milestones?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspear">SPEAR: Distilling Domain-Adaptive Reasoning Skeletons via Sequential Symbolic Alignment in Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pittsburgh</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Candidate process/format axes proxy milestones for LCS-F1. Teacher-text extraction is separate; known symbolic labels don&#x27;t prove extraction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Supplying symbols directly cannot test extracting them from a long proof.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26550">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.26550-spear/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b3521e591526d2b8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:v-rubrics" data-paper-title="V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-v-rubrics-b3920a4a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a0415fcdbddcdc16">What do VF, RC and IF measure in V-Rubrics?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Av-rubrics">V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · S-Lab, Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Visual faithfulness, reasoning consistency and instruction following. They are separate axes, not candidates or ordered steps; identify error type before assigning reward and prefix credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Wrong requested bullet count is IF; inventing an object is VF.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25580">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.25580-v-rubrics/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a0415fcdbddcdc16">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:v-rubrics" data-paper-title="V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f0e27b68376395a6">Why separate vision, reasoning and instruction following instead of one score?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Av-rubrics">V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · S-Lab, Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A visually correct reply can reason poorly; a coherent one may invent details. Atomic rubrics localize evidence to prefixes instead of obscuring it with terminal reward. Weights don&#x27;t validate labels; local proxies aren&#x27;t visual models.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Correct formatting doesn&#x27;t excuse a nonexistent object used as a premise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25580">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.25580-v-rubrics/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f0e27b68376395a6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:v-rubrics" data-paper-title="V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ccf69661c52bf587">Can V-Rubrics dimension weights replace criterion coverage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Av-rubrics">V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · S-Lab, Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Weights combine detected dimensions; coverage determines which errors are seen. Raising VF cannot penalize errors none of its rubrics detect. Objective tradeoff and measurement reliability differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Object-type-only checks may miss two becoming three regardless of VF weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25580">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.25580-v-rubrics/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ccf69661c52bf587">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:v-rubrics" data-paper-title="V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6165dbc62536173d">Do fixed V-Rubrics scores establish actual visual judging?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Av-rubrics">V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · S-Lab, Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Deterministic public candidates/plans test reward and credit without paper checkpoints, private data or full benchmarks. Fixed scores aren&#x27;t vision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A supplied VF score tests aggregation, not seeing an image.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25580">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.25580-v-rubrics/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6165dbc62536173d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:srpo" data-paper-title="SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-srpo-6cb8099c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bc9bdc2d6fcf7dc4">Why create a reflection patch after SRPO failure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asrpo">SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The patch converts coarse outcome feedback into privileged corrective context. The same model uses it to score actual student prefixes densely, not copy the failed trace.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After a tool error, a parameter-check reminder can guide teacher rescoring.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23493">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.23493-srpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bc9bdc2d6fcf7dc4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:srpo" data-paper-title="SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ceb50c358f897166">Why keep original rollout prefixes when a same-weight teacher sees a reflection patch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asrpo">SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The patch is hindsight training context for evaluating visited states. Rewriting student prefixes or giving the patch at deployment changes the task. Token teacher/old-student log ratios supply dense credit; reflection isn&#x27;t independently proven truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After a failed retrieval, a teacher may know the missed constraint while scoring, but the student didn&#x27;t know it during the original choice.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23493">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.23493-srpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ceb50c358f897166">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:srpo" data-paper-title="SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8963981c3086ad72">How does SRPO self-reflection differ from an independent external teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asrpo">SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Weights are shared and conditioning differs via feedback/patch, not additional parameters. A bad reflection can amplify shared bias; it isn&#x27;t independent verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Someone judging after seeing the outcome knows more, but isn&#x27;t a second expert.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23493">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.23493-srpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8963981c3086ad72">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:srpo" data-paper-title="SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1fbf4e7408760400">Should SRPO rescore a teacher-generated ideal prefix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asrpo">SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Keep actual student on-policy prefixes; patch changes teacher context only. Detach reward difference and advantage. Local proxy axes do not generate real patches or execute a large tool model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Score the student&#x27;s wrong third step as it occurred instead of replacing it with a correct one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23493">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.23493-srpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1fbf4e7408760400">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sa-mrpo" data-paper-title="Learn What&#x27;s Left, Not What&#x27;s Mastered: Saturation Aware Advantage Reweighting for Multi-Reward Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-sa-mrpo-184fd311" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a0af90db8872ed3b">Why track reward saturation in SA-MRPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asa-mrpo">Learn What&#x27;s Left, Not What&#x27;s Mastered: Saturation Aware Advantage Reweighting for Multi-Reward Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Florida</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Already mastered objectives can crowd out unlearned dimensions. Standardize each dimension and weight by one minus saturation; the saturation estimate must be meaningful.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If format nearly always passes, prioritize still-failing factual checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16072">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.16072-sa-mrpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a0af90db8872ed3b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sa-mrpo" data-paper-title="Learn What&#x27;s Left, Not What&#x27;s Mastered: Saturation Aware Advantage Reweighting for Multi-Reward Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-70571048b7377895">Why adjust weights based on saturation instead of always treating objectives equally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asa-mrpo">Learn What&#x27;s Left, Not What&#x27;s Mastered: Saturation Aware Advantage Reweighting for Multi-Reward Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Florida</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mastered dimensions can waste budget needed elsewhere. Normalize per dimension, then reduce saturated goals by a specified statistic. High scores don&#x27;t mean permanent mastery, and raw scale isn&#x27;t mastery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reduce formatting pressure if already solved, but check whether later reasoning training degrades it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16072">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.16072-sa-mrpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-70571048b7377895">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sa-mrpo" data-paper-title="Learn What&#x27;s Left, Not What&#x27;s Mastered: Saturation Aware Advantage Reweighting for Multi-Reward Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-72131cb19fdb4037">How does saturation weighting differ from fixed reward weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asa-mrpo">Learn What&#x27;s Left, Not What&#x27;s Mastered: Saturation Aware Advantage Reweighting for Multi-Reward Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Florida</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed weights ignore current mastery; saturation weighting adapts by batch. It doesn&#x27;t change ultimate importance or prevent forgetting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After downweighting a mastered skill, keep monitoring rather than declare it permanently solved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16072">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.16072-sa-mrpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-72131cb19fdb4037">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sa-mrpo" data-paper-title="Learn What&#x27;s Left, Not What&#x27;s Mastered: Saturation Aware Advantage Reweighting for Multi-Reward Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1d3549ed36ff2513">Can SA-MRPO compute one saturation after aggregating rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asa-mrpo">Learn What&#x27;s Left, Not What&#x27;s Mastered: Saturation Aware Advantage Reweighting for Multi-Reward Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Florida</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. That removes per-dimension budget allocation. Track each mean, variance and saturation before aggregation. Candidate formulas don&#x27;t reproduce checkpoint training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One aggregate hides low correctness and high format performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16072">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.16072-sa-mrpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1d3549ed36ff2513">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rubric-dropout" data-paper-title="Rubric Dropout: A Simple Way to Mitigate Reward Hacking in Rubric-as-Reward RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-rubric-dropout-0c8d1da7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5a48a08bd29cde14">Why randomly hide rubric criteria?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arubric-dropout">Rubric Dropout: A Simple Way to Mitigate Reward Hacking in Rubric-as-Reward RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Scale AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed proxies can be repeatedly exploited. Random subsets make a single shortcut unreliable. Hidden criteria are not unimportant; the visible reward composition changes during training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A canned phrase cannot reliably earn total reward if its easy criterion is often absent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.11669-rubric-dropout/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5a48a08bd29cde14">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rubric-dropout" data-paper-title="Rubric Dropout: A Simple Way to Mitigate Reward Hacking in Rubric-as-Reward RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ea048f226344f026">Why share a rubric subset within a rollout group?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arubric-dropout">Rubric Dropout: A Simple Way to Mitigate Reward Hacking in Rubric-as-Reward RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Scale AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Relative rewards need common criteria; different random criteria can misrank peers. Cross-group randomization reduces fixed shortcuts, but doesn&#x27;t guarantee valid remaining criteria or protect task performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Omit brevity for both answers, not only one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.11669-rubric-dropout/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ea048f226344f026">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rubric-dropout" data-paper-title="Rubric Dropout: A Simple Way to Mitigate Reward Hacking in Rubric-as-Reward RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c21118c94c319de5">How does group-shared dropout differ from independent masks per response?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arubric-dropout">Rubric Dropout: A Simple Way to Mitigate Reward Hacking in Rubric-as-Reward RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Scale AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared subset keeps same-prompt responses comparable. Independent masks confound quality with scoring criteria. Randomize by group.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Comparing A on format and B on correctness doesn&#x27;t isolate answer quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.11669-rubric-dropout/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c21118c94c319de5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rubric-dropout" data-paper-title="Rubric Dropout: A Simple Way to Mitigate Reward Hacking in Rubric-as-Reward RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b2ac7c4da469d607">When should Rubric Dropout sample and save the mask?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arubric-dropout">Rubric Dropout: A Simple Way to Mitigate Reward Hacking in Rubric-as-Reward RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Scale AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sample one mask per rollout group, freeze for scoring and log seed. Never choose masks after seeing which response benefits. No local real rubric judge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Hiding difficult criteria only after observing failure is cherry-picking, not dropout.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.11669-rubric-dropout/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b2ac7c4da469d607">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rrc" data-paper-title="RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-rrc-3d32cfb6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-aab7c26674050fe8">Why derive RRC generative reward from relative ranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arrc">RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northeastern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generative judges may compare reliably without calibrated standalone scores. Within-group ranks plus anchors yield centered rewards while exploiting comparative strength.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A judge may prefer one summary reliably but inconsistently use a ten-point scale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06310">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.06310-rrc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aab7c26674050fe8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rrc" data-paper-title="RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-efbd610af1123aeb">Why combine group and anchor ranking rather than ask for absolute scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arrc">RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northeastern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Comparative judgments can be more stable than absolute scale. Group competition gives relative position; anchors give cross-group reference before centering. This still depends on candidates and judge, not absolute truth or full paper evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two group winners may have very different quality relative to a shared anchor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06310">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.06310-rrc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-efbd610af1123aeb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rrc" data-paper-title="RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a6fd8d121f808e69">What do group self-competition and anchor ranks each provide?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arrc">RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northeastern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Group comparisons separate current candidates; anchors bridge groups where ranks alone hide absolute level. Specify weights; rank gaps aren&#x27;t equal quality distances.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An all-bad group still has a winner; an anchor can show it remains poor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06310">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.06310-rrc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a6fd8d121f808e69">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rrc" data-paper-title="RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-404cabbf88bd9a1e">Why check group size and rank direction before converting RRC ranks to rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arrc">RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northeastern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>K−1 requires more than one sample. Declare whether rank one is best. No local real judging or complete capability integration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A reversed formula can give the best rank the lowest reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06310">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.06310-rrc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-404cabbf88bd9a1e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:adrs" data-paper-title="ADRS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-adrs-2cc77780" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-60e05ad660e88f18">Why not simply trust high privileged-teacher confidence in ADRS?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadrs">ADRS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Extra skills/context may boost confidence without returns. Gate dense feedback by correlation between same-step teacher scores and observed returns.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher can favor a tool action that frequently fails.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03223">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.03223-adrs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-60e05ad660e88f18">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:adrs" data-paper-title="ADRS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e51841f6db85c131">Why check teacher confidence against realized return before using token guidance?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadrs">ADRS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Privileged certainty can amplify error. Normalize within interaction steps, gate by positive return association and use the existing reward-to-advantage path. Negative association isn&#x27;t help; inference does not use privileged training skill/outcome.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Gate out confidence in fluent but ineffective tool calls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03223">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.03223-adrs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e51841f6db85c131">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:adrs" data-paper-title="ADRS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a89350278459cda5">How does TVA correlation gating differ from fixed distillation weight?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadrs">ADRS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed weight always trusts teacher; positive correlation retains signals associated with returns. Batch correlation is not causality and may not use test gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If teacher scores don&#x27;t track success, extra guidance weakens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03223">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.03223-adrs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a89350278459cda5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:adrs" data-paper-title="ADRS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-29657d9aa8a6b890">Does ADRS standardize over a full trajectory or within interaction steps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadrs">ADRS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Standardize teacher scores within each interaction step and correlate across trajectory returns, then feed host reward-to-advantage logic. Local z-scores aren&#x27;t correctness labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare second tool calls with other second calls, not every turn combined.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03223">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.03223-adrs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-29657d9aa8a6b890">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:serpo" data-paper-title="SERPO: Self-Evolving Rubric Policy Optimization for Open-Ended Test-Time Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-serpo-1bbe9fff" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c2866c0ae1401306">Why keep a Good–Normal–Bad archive in SERPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aserpo">SERPO: Self-Evolving Rubric Policy Optimization for Open-Ended Test-Time Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different qualities inform prompt-specific rubrics and policy learning. Actor and criteria evolve; storing only highest scores loses contrasts. Classification depends on judge quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Medium answers expose gaps and bad answers show patterns to avoid.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26873">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.26873-serpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c2866c0ae1401306">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:serpo" data-paper-title="SERPO: Self-Evolving Rubric Policy Optimization for Open-Ended Test-Time Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-40eccd1b65b34ba5">Why separate SERPO archive, rubric and actor roles?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aserpo">SERPO: Self-Evolving Rubric Policy Optimization for Open-Ended Test-Time Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The archive stores comparisons, rubric defines current standards, and actor generates. Feedback can adapt or amplify bias. New archive or rubric doesn&#x27;t itself train or improve the model; use independent holdout.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A short-only archive, brevity rubric and short actor may agree while neglecting facts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26873">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.26873-serpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-40eccd1b65b34ba5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:serpo" data-paper-title="SERPO: Self-Evolving Rubric Policy Optimization for Open-Ended Test-Time Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-54db0361417a9679">How does SERPO differ from repeated RL under a fixed rubric?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aserpo">SERPO: Self-Evolving Rubric Policy Optimization for Open-Ended Test-Time Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It updates query-specific rubrics and archives with the actor. Fixed criteria can lose discrimination, but coevolution risks drift and self-reinforcement. Self-scores aren&#x27;t proof.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>New criteria can distinguish harder negatives after the actor learns initial rules.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26873">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.26873-serpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-54db0361417a9679">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:serpo" data-paper-title="SERPO: Self-Evolving Rubric Policy Optimization for Open-Ended Test-Time Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb6638f64a00a344">How should SERPO track its three evolving states?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aserpo">SERPO: Self-Evolving Rubric Policy Optimization for Open-Ended Test-Time Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Record versions and ordering of generation, archive, rubric and actor updates. Don&#x27;t retrospectively score with later rubrics. Local candidates don&#x27;t implement full generation/judging.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Log the actual rubric used for each batch so training supervision is auditable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26873">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.26873-serpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb6638f64a00a344">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cort" data-paper-title="CoRT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-cort-3a4a9a75" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-930c953e3f0bce85">Why replay one reply with and without criteria in CoRT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acort">CoRT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance internship</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep response fixed so likelihood differences link rubric context to token positions, redistributing response advantage rather than adding another global score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A format requirement can affect bracket tokens and their credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.25659-cort/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-930c953e3f0bce85">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cort" data-paper-title="CoRT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-771f392e93e7712c">Why replay the same response instead of generating separately under each rubric view?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acort">CoRT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance internship</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed tokens/prefixes isolate conditioning better; regenerating also changes trajectories. Use the difference to allocate original advantage, not pass scoring text into deployment. Counterfactual contexts can still bias the estimate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A citation token&#x27;s likelihood can change with a citation requirement; regenerating the whole paragraph adds other changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.25659-cort/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-771f392e93e7712c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cort" data-paper-title="CoRT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-10c4f02fc797746e">How does CoRT counterfactual replay differ from attention weighting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acort">CoRT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance internship</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Replay changes evaluation context and compares probabilities; attention measures one forward&#x27;s information weights. Neither directly proves causality; attention isn&#x27;t the specified contrast.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high-attention token may show unchanged likelihood when criteria are removed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.25659-cort/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-10c4f02fc797746e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cort" data-paper-title="CoRT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9bee9b91adbf24e5">Why align both CoRT scoring passes to the same token and prefix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acort">CoRT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance internship</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different generated text confounds the criteria intervention. Normalized weights scale fixed advantage; original student sampling must not see the privileged rubric. Candidate features aren&#x27;t token replay.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scoring sentence A with criteria and B without doesn&#x27;t isolate their effect.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.25659-cort/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9bee9b91adbf24e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tcr" data-paper-title="TCR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-tcr-a5ef9cee" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ba053d62fb8e7cba">Why subtract outcome EMA from TCR process scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atcr">TCR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Process and outcome can double-reward success. The residual captures improvement not already explained by outcome before combining them. EMA is training state, not item truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A correct answer should not automatically earn the same success signal again through process scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19824">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.19824-tcr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ba053d62fb8e7cba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tcr" data-paper-title="TCR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-28193c59a175f590">Why subtract a moving outcome baseline rather than add both rewards directly?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atcr">TCR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Process ratings often track correctness, so direct sums can count success twice. The moving residual attempts to isolate extra reasoning benefit. It depends on checklist and baseline quality, and local proxies don&#x27;t establish full reasoning performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If correct answers routinely earn high process scores, only an improvement beyond the usual outcome level gives new evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19824">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.19824-tcr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-28193c59a175f590">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tcr" data-paper-title="TCR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-871611a87be6887c">How does TCR residual differ from adding process and outcome rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atcr">TCR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Addition accumulates both signals. Subtracting a dynamic outcome baseline reduces duplicate credit. It does not prove exact decorrelation or remove judge bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A higher outcome baseline reduces extra credit for an unchanged process score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19824">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.19824-tcr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-871611a87be6887c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tcr" data-paper-title="TCR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-742d03a7a9c6d3b5">Does local TCR call a model to generate per-example checklists?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atcr">TCR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Candidate policies test residual computation, not real checklist generation or free-text training. Update EMA in training order, not from test performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A hand-provided checklist does not validate automatic checklist quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19824">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.19824-tcr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-742d03a7a9c6d3b5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dynamic-rubric" data-paper-title="Co-Evolving LLM Evaluators and Policies via DynamicRubric" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-dynamic-rubric-5fe56c96" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ec541e2997598ca">Why build DynamicRubric criteria from the current candidate set?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adynamic-rubric">Co-Evolving LLM Evaluators and Policies via DynamicRubric</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat / Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Old rules can saturate after policy gains. New hard negatives need discriminating dimensions and weights, while anchors limit judge drift. Not permission to change rules after outcomes arbitrarily.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Once every answer meets formatting, look for evidence that still separates quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20083">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.20083-dynamic-rubric/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ec541e2997598ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dynamic-rubric" data-paper-title="Co-Evolving LLM Evaluators and Policies via DynamicRubric" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-59f9cc11b48a7651">Why balance hard-negative discrimination and anchoring?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adynamic-rubric">Co-Evolving LLM Evaluators and Policies via DynamicRubric</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat / Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed rubrics can stop separating improved replies; dynamic dimensions help. Discrimination alone can learn stylistic shortcuts, so an anchor stabilizes the reference. Coevolution is not objective improvement without independent tests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>When formatting saturates, new criteria should not simply favor verbosity unchecked.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20083">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.20083-dynamic-rubric/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-59f9cc11b48a7651">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dynamic-rubric" data-paper-title="Co-Evolving LLM Evaluators and Policies via DynamicRubric" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-78a5fcd1bb4f3dc8">How do discrimination and anchoring pull DynamicRubric in different directions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adynamic-rubric">Co-Evolving LLM Evaluators and Policies via DynamicRubric</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat / Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Discrimination increases sensitivity to current hard cases; anchors retain prior standards and deter co-adaptation. Either alone can reward irrelevant differences or preserve stale criteria.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Length is easy to distinguish, but an anchor should constrain it if unrelated to quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20083">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.20083-dynamic-rubric/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-78a5fcd1bb4f3dc8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dynamic-rubric" data-paper-title="Co-Evolving LLM Evaluators and Policies via DynamicRubric" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7573cde7b2242058">Why tie DynamicRubric weights to prompt and candidate version?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adynamic-rubric">Co-Evolving LLM Evaluators and Policies via DynamicRubric</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat / Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both determine scoring and new candidates may imply new criteria. Log rubric and anchor versions; don&#x27;t compare rewards under undeclared weight changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Score changes across two rounds can reflect changed criteria, not actor gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20083">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.20083-dynamic-rubric/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7573cde7b2242058">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:taco" data-paper-title="TACO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-taco-d0adf0d1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c59506c22db1e018">Why can a correct TACO response contain tokens that shouldn&#x27;t be reinforced?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ataco">TACO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Johns Hopkins University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal correctness only validates the result. Uniform positive credit can reinforce lucky or implausible intermediate tokens. Tail risk smoothly reduces their positive contribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A correct computation with a false explanation is not wholly exemplary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.07976">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.07976-taco/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c59506c22db1e018">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:taco" data-paper-title="TACO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
